recipes.name: Magical Egg Salad
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, remove from heat, and let eggs stand in hot water for 15 minutes. Remove eggs from hot water, cool under cold running water, and peel.
Chop eggs and transfer to a large bowl.
Stir mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, sweet pickle relish, steak sauce, paprika, and dill into eggs until well mixed; season with salt and black pepper. Cover and refrigerate until chilled, if desired.
Sprinkle with cayenne pepper before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Magical Egg Salad
raw_recipe.description: The magic in the simple egg salad is a splash of steak sauce.

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make a magical egg salad with a secret ingredient that really brings it all together. After boiling and chopping the eggs, mix them together with the usual egg salad ingredients like mayo, dijon mustard, sweet relish, and seasoning. Finally, add the secret ingredient to give it some extra tanginess: steak sauce. Serve this savory egg salad on toasted bread for a decadent lunch meal!

review.reviewBody: PLEASE FELLOW AR USERS, PLEASE DO NOT RATE A DISH WHEN YOU HAVE ALTERED THE RECIPE AS IT DOES LITTLE TO HELP OTHERS THAT WISH TO TRY A POSTED RECIPE. :D Don't want to come off like a butt but it drives me nuts to see a posted recipe than a user saying deleted this/added that/changed this to that UGH I made it as listed and while magical is not the word I would use I would call it a refreshing twist to the standard egg salad recipe. The addition of steak sauce brought a nice flip to the standard and came off well. I would definitely use this again. I substituted boiled fish heads for eggs and added a light balsamic glaze while mixing JUST KIDDING I followed it as listed and it was pretty good.

A good combination of ingredients, but. My biggest peeve with egg salad is the egg whites being too large. Something about large chunks of whites with mayo, it's just slimy. My method for chopping is by using a pastry cutter on the eggs which combines the yolk and whites into almost a fine powder. When the other ingredients are combined the mixture turns into a wonderful moist spread with all the richness and flavor you're looking for without slimy whites. Give it a whirl. I'll bet you like it. P.S. Adding crunchy bacon bits just before serving puts this over the top.

Despise sweet relish so used dill pickle relish instead, and have no other use for steak sauce so substituted it with Worchester sauce (although, they're not exactly interchangeable) and used smoked paprika, which I love in almost everything (plain paprika has no taste). Very good! These are not "tweaks", just substitutions.

I made this a little differently but I think it's the best egg salad yet. I left out relish as I don't care for the texture in egg salad. I also left out the dillweed. I did add about 2 to 3 tsp pickle juice. I also add a lot of pepper. The a1, paprika, and cayenne create a great flavor!

Making for lunch today so giving it a 5 star as a start and only thing I plan differently is addition of celery - because I have some I need to use. Mainly wanted to say that I absolutely LOVE reading comments from those who have adjusted recipes. Very rarely do I follow a recipe to a "t" and its helpful to see what other suggest - not just in ingredients but also methods. I've learned quite a few new tricks from commenters. One I'll be using today and that is to use my small squared cooling rack to push the eggs through. Makes perfect pieces for egg salads - IMHO UPDATE: I wanted to update my review after making the egg salad. The only change was to add small diced celery and green onion. It was a hit. So my 5 stars stand.

Very close to my mom's egg salad flavor. I finely diced a white onion (just a tablespoon or so) to add a bit more crunch than the relish adds. I substituted a few squirts of Frank's Red Hot sauce as I didn't have A-1 steak sauce. Came out pretty nice! Recommend staying with the basics if you haven't made before, and then adding more to it. Don't oversalt!

First, steak sauce and dijon mustard does not go in a GOOD Egg Salad, but, I made it just like the recipe states and everyone said that it stunk and not to make it for them again. Made it minus steak sauce and dijon mustard and everyone loved it. I used Sweet Salad Cubes and I put a little Heinz Yellow Mustard and it was also good.

Sometimes I make egg salad using a touch of yellow curry and/or real bacon bits... afterall, bacon and eggs go together. Thought I'd try this version. I used 7 large eggs and adjusted other ingredients a touch. I also added 1 chopped celery rib for a little crunch. After I got it all together I wasn't impressed but after 24 hours in the fridge, the flavors developed... excellent with crackers and on seeded rye bread.

I don't like to peel eggs, I'm really messy with that! Instead, I crack the eggs open into either a muffin pan, with muffin paper cups for easy clean up. Then I bake them at 350º F until done-about 17 minutes, and cut them up. Both the whites & yolk are set and not runny. I also do this for eggs in potato salads. For breakfast for a crowd, I cook them for 14 minutes for a runny yolk, and adjust baking time for firmer eggs. Saves so much time! I bake bacon or Canadian bacon & sausages the same way, all at once and everything is hot at the same time.
I only did 3 eggs as it’s only me to try this. I adjusted the amounts, and was quite surprised how good it tasted. Will definitely to do this one again.
2 tablespoons of Dijon mustard was too much. It overpowered the other flavors. If I decide to make this again I will cut that in half.
I made this exactly as written. My husband and I both loved it! Thanks for sharing.

An absolute success!!! We both love egg salad but this one had just the right variances - steak sauce (used A-1) for depth and zing, Dijon mustard, and cayenne for a hint of heat!!! The rest of the ingredients are what I usually use. No modifications needed and not adding garlic or onion powder (which I usually do) gave it enough of a variance from my normal summer egg dishes (deviled eggs, potato salad, etc) to be a real standout 😁

I made a couple of changes, added Worcester sauce in place of steak seasoning , added one celery stalk, finely chopped. Bread, used Keto bread to reduce the carbs to 1 to 4 grams per slice instead of 15 carbs per slice for regular bread. Lastly, I sliced a ripe tomato from the farm stand , thinly sliced, layered one piece of bread then topped with my egg salad. You’re going to love it.
Really easy and good. I would add green onions chopped thinly.
I will try the steak sauce in my egg salad but not the sweet pickles. I hate them! I will use dill pickles only. Taste much better in my opinion.

Basically, that is how I make deviled eggs. I use A1, Dijon mustard, mayo, salt n pepper to my egg yolks. Stuff my egg white. Sometimes I add a little horseradish instead of Dijon and use regular mustard. Either way, it is very good.
I made some tweaks. It is great.

I used everything as listed and it was totally amazing. The steak sauce i used was my husband's favorite heinz 57 and wow. The flavor totally surprised me. I've made a few more times and yup totally a keeper!
I made this, but instead of steak sauce, I used Worcestershire sauce and a dash of lemon juice for a little extra flavor. It was delicious.
